name: outpatient_encounters
description: Synthetic adult primary-care outpatient encounters with a structured summary and a clinician note.
context:
Primary-care clinic in the US. Notes follow a SOAP structure (Subjective, Objective, Assessment,
Plan), written in terse clinical shorthand with standard abbreviations (pt, hx, c/o, SOB, BP, f/u).
Vitals in the note must match the structured fields exactly. Diagnoses must be consistent with age,
sex, symptoms and vitals; medications must be appropriate first-line choices with plausible doses.
Include realistic comorbidities for older patients (HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia, CKD).
All names, dates and identifiers are fictional.

fields.name: medications_prescribed
fields.description: New or changed prescriptions, e.g. 'lisinopril 10 mg PO daily'.

rules: Vital signs in the note must match systolic_bp, diastolic_bp, heart_rate and temperature_c exactly.
Diagnoses must be supported by the note's findings; the first diagnosis is the primary one.
Preventive visits for patients under 40 rarely have more than one diagnosis.
systolic_bp is greater than diastolic_bp by at least 20.
checks: str(systolic_bp) in note and str(heart_rate) in note

diversity.scenario_guidance: Span common primary-care presentations across organ systems, from URIs and back pain to chest pain work-ups, depression screening, diabetes management and pre-travel visits.
